summary: U.S. equities rebounded Friday after a sharp selloff, with the S&P 500 rising 0.6% and the Dow adding 0.9% as Treasury markets stabilized following Treasury Secretary Bessent's announcement to double long-term debt buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation. The move, aimed at calming bond market volatility after 30-year yields hit nearly 20-year highs earlier this week, failed to fully reassure investors on Thursday but sparked a risk-on rally Friday. Bitcoin surged near $77,000, posting its best weekly gain in over three years, fueled by Trump's renewed push for the Clarity Act and declining Treasury yields. Crypto-linked equities rallied in tandem, with Strategy and Bitmine gaining around 10%. Meanwhile, Walmart shares plunged 9.2% after reporting its slowest quarterly sales growth in over six years, weighing on retail sentiment. Geopolitical tensions with Iran escalated as President Trump announced plans for "economic warfare," adding an overhang to risk assets. The Philadelphia Fed Index beat expectations at 47.4, signaling manufacturing strength, though investors remain cautious heading into a light data week.

signals.title: Treasury doubles debt buybacks to calm bond market
signals.desc: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced at least $4 billion in long-term debt repurchases, pushing yields lower and supporting risk assets including equities and crypto.

signals.title: Bitcoin surges to $77,000 on Trump crypto push
signals.desc: Bitcoin posted its best weekly gain in three years as Trump urged Congress to pass the Clarity Act, with Ethereum jumping 17.5% and nearly $3 billion in short liquidations fueling the rally.

signals.title: Walmart posts slowest sales growth in six years
signals.desc: Walmart shares fell 9.2% after reporting the slowest quarterly sales growth since 2020, raising concerns about consumer spending and retail earnings quality.

signals.title: Trump declares economic warfare on Iran
signals.desc: Escalating geopolitical tensions as Trump threatens Iran with economic measures, pushing oil prices higher and adding risk-off pressure to equities on Thursday.

signals.title: Philadelphia Fed Index beats at 47.4
signals.desc: August manufacturing gauge topped estimates and July's 41.4 reading, signaling resilience but failing to offset broader bond market and geopolitical concerns.

verdict: Treasury intervention and crypto-friendly policy signals are driving a fragile risk-on rally, but geopolitical tensions and retail weakness keep bulls on guard.
